SearchAliases: to spare someone is not folly
letting someone off is not stupidity
Senses.Note: Case appraisal, letting one move pass, declining a penalty, and conduct instruction all preserve deliberate restraint as the shared act.

Occurrences.Kwic: 何事臨場欠作家？祇緣別有好生涯。饒人不是癡男女，最毒於菟無齒牙。

Occurrences.Kwic: 有人辨得，許你天下橫行。神鼎僼云：叢林商量，盡道知恩報恩，殊不知落在驢前馬後。若是天童，便與摩頂授記。善哉，善哉！如是，如是！不妨遞代相傳。龍華體云：韶陽雖則據令，終是賊過張弓。若要天下太平，不如放過一着。何故饒人不是癡？崇先奇云：總謂雲門跨竈也是疾行，先長臯亭也與雲門一棒，貴圖兩得相見，爾等還甘麼？萬壽範云：黃面老子固已誇大而涉險，跛足阿師豈非忠耿而蹈譏？仔細檢點將來，二者皆為不了。何故？不見道：天下有道，則庶人不議。洞山昱云：世尊手忙脚亂，自生驚怪。雲門棒雖有眼

Occurrences.Kwic: 雖然如是，放過也好。會麼？饒人不是癡漢。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1414.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Liao’an Qingyu. Liao'an Qingyu says that letting the interlocutor off is good, then quotes the proverb.

Senses.Explanation: This proverb says that deliberately sparing a person or letting a move pass is not foolishness. A verse applies it to leaving an opponent alive; Longhua Ti joins it to letting one move pass, Liao’an Qingyu uses it after declining the full penalty, and Cishou Huaishen uses it in instruction to endure insult rather than retaliate.
